transcript.content: Hello, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, what brings me in is that I've just... I've completely stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. 

It's gotten pretty bad lately. I usually love going out to salsa nights, or heading to the church gatherings, or even just cooking for my neighbors. But I haven't been doing any of it. I just don't have it in me. I'm a carpenter, and lately... I don't even want to walk out into my own shop just to enjoy the smell of the wood. I just don't care about any of it right now.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been about two months now. It really started when my wife's health suddenly declined. Our whole routine changed, and... well, that's when this whole shift in my mood and behavior began.
Since this began, have you felt sad or down most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah, I have. Pretty much every day. Most mornings I wake up with this... this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. It's hard to describe, but it's like all the color has just gone out of the house. I spend a lot of the day just having to force myself not to break down in front of my wife. So, yes, I've been feeling very down.
Before your wife’s health declined, had you ever experienced a similar period of persistent sadness and loss of interest lasting at least two weeks?

Well... actually, now that you ask it that way, yes. I know I just said two months, but if I really think back to before she even got sick, I was already slipping into this. 

Honestly, this whole thing has been dragging on for about six months now. Her health declining just made it a lot harder to ignore. But yeah, it's been going on long enough that it definitely no longer feels like just a bad week or ordinary stress.
Before this six-month period began, had you ever had another distinct period of depression that later fully improved?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I've had rough patches before, sure, just regular stress from work or life. But nothing like this. Before this started about six months ago, I never had a time where I felt this down and empty for weeks on end. This is really the first time it's been anything like this.
Have you had thoughts of killing yourself or not wanting to be alive?

Yes, I have. I mean... I've had thoughts that maybe it would just be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. Just go to sleep and not have to face it all. And sometimes I catch myself thinking my family might actually be better off without me having to drag them down. It honestly scares me a bit that my mind goes there, but... yeah, I've been having those thoughts.
How has your energy been during this period?

It's been pretty much non-existent. I mean... even after just sitting down for a while or getting a full night in bed, my body feels completely worn out. It feels like I've been framing a roof all day long, even when I haven't really done anything. Just the small stuff, like... loading my tools into the truck... it just feels like it's way too much to handle right now. I just don't have it in me.
How much has this depression interfered with your ability to work and manage your usual daily responsibilities?

It's interfered a lot, to be honest. At work, I've actually had to hand off parts of the jobs I normally supervise myself. I just can't keep up with it right now. And outside of work... I've pretty much pulled away from everyone. I don't go to church, I don't talk to my friends or the neighbors anymore. I've isolated myself so much that my wife and the contact at our parish actually got worried about my safety.
Have you been having trouble concentrating or making decisions during this period?

Yeah, I have. It's... well, I'll sit there staring at blueprints I've been reading my whole life, and the lines just kind of blur together in my head. I can't seem to make sense of them right now. I actually end up having to ask the younger guys on the crew to repeat things that I should understand right away. My brain just won't focus on it.
